For more than a month now, we have been spending Wednesday evenings with the École Converse cohort at the Forum Jeunesse de Saint-Michel. With Ahmed, Fatima, Naila and Marc, our budding journalists, we are covering the basics of dialogue journalism. We are delighted to let them introduce themselves today.
<strong>Fatima Bah, par Marc Elder Piar<: Fatima Bah, by Marc Elder PiarTo understand who Fatima is today, you have to go back to her childhood. Her strong social involvement and great intellectual curiosity don’t come out of nowhere. She was lucky enough to be raised in a Pan-African family. From a young age, her parents instilled in her a love for her community. Little by little, Fatima developed a particular interest in the history of Black and African communities. That is how, today, we discover that she has become a committed young woman. Fatima knows her history and is proud of it. She believes nothing will change if we don’t get involved in the struggle.Read Fatima’s first report here.‍

‍<strong>Marc Piard Elder, par Fatima Ba: ‍Marc Piard Elder, by Fatima Bah A great lover of general knowledge, Marc has an easy time understanding the world around him. It is thanks to this quality that he was able to overcome the obstacles that stood in his way when he arrived in Quebec three years ago, in the middle of the pandemic. This young man quickly adapted to his new environment, and his social involvement in his community and at his school contributed greatly to that. Today, Marc makes the rounds of Montréal’s many debate clubs to meet new people and hone his public speaking. Next fall, he plans to pursue law studies at university so he can follow in the footsteps of the great men who inspire him: “Men who are ready to die for their cause, like Thomas Sangara,” he says.

<strong>‍</strong>Depuis qu’il est tout: ‍Since he was very young, Ahmed has been interested in the world of multimedia. He spends many hours doing graphic design and learning to use editing software like Photoshop. Eager to help others and connect with them, he manages to do so through this medium. Reserved by nature, he expresses his desire for innovation and his creativity through his art. Ahmed draws a lot of inspiration from young people who, like him, succeed at what they undertake. That is also what drives him to constantly work on new projects and push himself further. Who knows, tomorrow he might be the owner of Tesla or Twitter! His motto is a line from the rapper Youssoupha: “If you can’t do great things, you have to do small things with greatness.”
